WGUS86 KSEW 110647
FLSSEW

Flood Statement
National Weather Service Seattle WA
1047 PM PST Wed Dec 10 2025

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in 
Washington...

  Skagit River Near Mt. Vernon affecting Skagit County.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in 
Washington...

  Skagit River Near Concrete affecting Skagit County.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood 
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the 
dangers of flooding.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet 
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim, 
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters, 
stop, turn around and go another way.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive 
cars through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued by Thursday morning at 700 AM PST.

1047 PM PST Wed Dec 10 2025

...FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL EARLY SATURDAY AFTERNOON...

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. 
  This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skagit River near Mt. Vernon.

* WHEN...Until early Saturday afternoon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
  - At 10:15 PM PST Wednesday the stage was 29.0 feet.
  - Flood stage is 28.0 feet.
  - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
    ending at 10:15 PM PST Wednesday was 29.0 feet.
  - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 41.3
    feet late Friday morning. It will then fall below flood stage
    early Saturday morning.
  - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
